title: Honey Potion: An eBPF Backend for Elixir
problem: eBPF programs are currently compiled from Restricted C or from bindings in other languages, but lack support for functional programming languages. Translation to eBPF requires satisfying strict verifier constraints including bounded memory access and termination proofs.
motivation: Extending eBPF to functional languages enables broader developer accessibility and allows leveraging functional programming benefits (immutability, composability) for kernel-level systems programming.
method: Honey Potion compiler translates Elixir to eBPF binaries by leveraging the verifier's termination requirement to enable optimizations: constant propagation, type specialization, and partial evaluation. Ensures semantics preservation and verifier acceptance through compile-time proof strategies.
key_novelty: First compiler for a functional programming language to eBPF, creatively leveraging verifier termination constraints for optimization.
contributions: First functional language (Elixir) to eBPF compiler
Leverages termination requirement for constant propagation, type specialization, partial evaluation
Publicly available and used in production (packet routers, process monitors, event loggers)
Enables functional programming paradigm for kernel-space applications
baselines: Existing eBPF compilers from C/Rust/Python bindings
limitations: Performance evaluation and optimization effectiveness not discussed in abstract.
